name: persistence_normalise
description: Scheduled tasks linked to their registration and execution evidence, without a persistence verdict. Inputs, any of which may be given (at least software or tasks_dir): software, the SOFTWARE hive (TaskCache: Tree, Tasks, Plain, Boot, Logon, Maintenance); tasks_dir, a directory of Task Scheduler XML files (Windows\System32\Tasks, walked without following links; a pipe, a link or another non-regular entry is counted and never opened; a file over 8 MiB is refused); evtx_results, an evtx_query result file (JSON Lines; there is no import of other tools). One item per task path, with its registration evidence (xml, tree, tree_sd, tasks_key: present, absent or not_provided; the Plain, Boot, Logon and Maintenance groups), the XML fields with locators (URI, author, date, principal, trigger kinds, each action's kind, command, arguments, working directory; at most 50 actions listed, the rest counted), the TaskCache Actions and Triggers values as bytes (actions_hex, triggers_hex, not decoded: the XML is the readable definition), and DynamicInfo decoded by its length (28 or 36 bytes) and first number (2 or 3) with the layout and its basis (unsupported, bytes kept, when it fits neither). Task XML is UTF-16, UTF-8 or UTF-16BE read by its byte order mark; a DOCTYPE or ENTITY declaration is refused before any parse, so no entity is ever expanded, and malformed XML is refused with a fixed reason (xml_refused). Observations are facts about the inputs, never verdicts: xml_without_taskcache, taskcache_without_xml, tree_entry_without_sd_value (the shape a hidden task has), tree_entry_without_tasks_key, tasks_key_without_tree_entry, events_only; they are only stated when both sides were provided. Execution evidence is filled only from evtx_results: Security 4698 to 4702 and Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational 106, 140, 141, 200 and 201, matched to a task by the TaskName data field, case-insensitively; at most 200 events are listed per task, the rest are counted (events_not_listed). WMI repository: not examined; permanent subscriptions are never read. The offsets of DynamicInfo are those the published notes give and are not verified against a real hive. Second reader: NOT DONE. No RECmd, RegRipper or Dissect reader is started; nothing in the answer is cross-checked by an independent reader. The hive is read as it is: hive_dirty comes from the base block's sequence numbers and the transaction logs beside the hive are named and not replayed; every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive. Problems are a page (the first 40 inline, all in all_problems); the items are a page (limit inline, the whole result as JSON Lines named in all_results, never replaced by a smaller one). The tool stops at its own time limit (294 seconds) and says partial, naming how many entries were not read or written; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file. status is complete only when every file, key and line named was read and decoded: a refused task file, an unsupported DynamicInfo, a problem, events past the listing, a skipped link or pipe, a time stop and a blind filter each make it partial, and status_basis says which. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (paths, names, publishers and hashes): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). ORDER: the items are taken in the order of the text shown for each task path (withheld paths in an order of their own that is new for every run), not the order the hive or the directory stores them. FILTER: `contains` is looked for in the text the answer prints for the task path, the URI, and each action's command and arguments (never in what the boundary withheld); an item not matched whose printed text holds a withheld part is counted (contains_blind_records) and makes the answer partial, because the needle may be in what is withheld; the name of a result file never depends on the filter's text. Command and Arguments of a task can carry secrets: they are withheld by shape like every other text, and the full text is in the values file only in a job run as secret output. A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Past the judging time (SEAL_BUDGET, 10 seconds for an answer or a row, and never past the seal stop of the tool, which is 3.5 seconds before its time limit because the string being judged at that point is finished first and one string of 256 KiB can take up to 2.3 seconds) the strings the evidence supplied are no longer judged: each is replaced whole by <withheld N bytes: backstop: the judging time ran out>, counted and listed, and the answer is partial, except the names this tool wrote itself (its keys, the names of its result files, the name of the hive, its status basis) and a string of 15 characters or fewer made only of letters, digits, _ and . that does not start like a vendor token and, in a field of a typed kind (a SID, a GUID, a digest), fits the grammar of its type (so not a Slack-shaped token, not the value after a flag such as -pwd, not a prefix and 12 characters). The seal stop ends the judging only, not the tool's own work, which has its own, earlier clock. When any part of a free-text string is withheld, the line breaks, tabs and invisible characters of that string are not kept in the text shown (it is judged without them); a string with nothing withheld is shown exactly as it is. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape, five independent runs, 4,940 per shape; rates, not guarantees; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes: 0 printed whole in 4,940 plants of each shape and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: about 0.1% printed whole (0 whole and 1 piece of 12 characters in 4,940 plants of the block's own harness; 1 of 105 canaries end to end, the same canary in four slots; an earlier measurement found 2 whole and 3 pieces in 4,940), so the rate is small and not zero. The shapes that are not zero, as the range of the five runs over all slots with the worst single slot (76 plants, one plant is 1.3%) beside it: 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 1.3%; up to 3.9% in end-to-end runs); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24 9.2% to 10.6% (worst slot 14.5% to 21.1%); a 16-character base32 seed 9.8% to 11.7% (worst slot 15.8% to 21.1%). In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Strings changed (any part withheld) on real evidence: in a real 72 MB SOFTWARE hive (3,000 strings sampled per class) 3.7% of key-name components, 1.0% of value names and 0.9% of REG_SZ data (the names of the Windows component store, WinSxS, are not replaced by the backstop in a name, key or path); in real event logs (175 logs, 64,716 records, up to 4 MB each) the XML of 2.0% of the records is replaced whole by the backstop (5.6% before the shape guard of this round; Security 0.1%, was 6.7%), 1.7% of the data fields are withheld (3.7% before, process ids no longer) and 45 of the 175 runs end partial (84 before). The average hides channels: PowerShell/Operational has the XML of 25.0% of its 1,857 records replaced whole (script blocks carry base64 and long identifiers) and CodeIntegrity/Operational 33.3% of its 1,309 (event 3089, whose Hash is a padded base64 digest). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 69% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true.

software.description: Path to the SOFTWARE hive (the TaskCache)

tasks_dir.description: Path to a directory of Task Scheduler XML files (Windows/System32/Tasks of the collection)

evtx_results.description: Path to an evtx_query result file (JSON Lines) holding Security 4698 to 4702 and TaskScheduler/Operational 106, 140, 141, 200, 201

contains.description: Keep items whose printed path, URI, command or arguments contain this text, case-insensitively; looked for only in the text the answer prints

limit.description: Items shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); every item is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
